newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas craters late, Mar off sharply.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas craters late, Mar off sharply.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, hit by a late wave of selling Friday, ended lower across the board, pressured by softer physical prices and forecasts for milder temperatures next week, sources said.
March tumbled 10.1 cents to close at $2.385 per million British thermal units. April settled 7.6 cents lower at $2.139. Other deferreds ended down by one-half to 5.5 cents.

"The longs were hoping for a technical rally and it didn't meterialize, so they dumped it. There's some mild weather coming, and we could gap lower Monday," said one Midwest trader, adding early-Feb cash should stay soft.
Weather Services Corp expects Midwest and eastern temperatures mostly to range from normal to above-normal next week, with weather in Texas and the Southeast also forecast to climb to above normal.
With eastern utilities already giving back gas for early in the month, few expected the market to rally far without some sustained cold in the Midwest and South.

"I think the market is heading to full contango unless colder weather materializes in the Midcontinent and South," the Midwest trader said, referring to expectations that front-to-back spreads would continue to narrow near-term.

Technically, traders now pegged support in March at the December 30 low of $2.35, with many expecting it to give way early next week unless colder weather shows up. Resistance was seen at $2.70 and $2.80.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices slipped Friday by about a dime to the mid-$2.70s. Midcon pipes tumbled more than 20 cents to about the $2.50 level. New York city gate gas skidded 15 cents into the mid-$3.40s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell 3.4 cents to $2.162. NYMEX said an estimated 21,460 Hub contracts traded, down from Thursday's revised tally of 28,080.
NYMEX Alberta natgas traded 15 lots Friday, while Permian again was untraded.

On the KCBT, March finished five cents lower at $2.14, while deferreds ended mixed. The East/West spread narrowed by 5.1 cents to 24.5 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 103 contracts traded, up from Thursday's total of 33.
